html:
Thomas Warner was the English captain who founded the first English colony in the Caribbean, on St Kitts, in 1624. He governed it until his death in 1649.

French settlers under Pierre Belain d'Esnambuc arrived in 1625, and the two nations shared the island. Together they attacked the Kalinago in the massacre of 1626.

From St Kitts, Warner's men settled Nevis, Antigua and Montserrat, so the island is called the mother colony of the English Caribbean. Tobacco came first, then sugar worked by enslaved Africans. His son by a Kalinago woman, Indian Warner, later led Kalinago on Dominica.
